body.p: This Data Processing Agreement ("DPA") is effective {{effective}} between **{{customer}}**, {{customer_entity}} with its principal place of business at {{customer_address}}, {{customer_city}}, {{customer_region}} {{customer_postal}} ("Customer", the controller), and {{fontara_entity}} ("Vendor", the processor), and forms part of the Master Services Agreement between them dated {{msa_date}} (the "Agreement").

"Personal Data" means information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person that Vendor processes on Customer's behalf under the Agreement, as described in Annex I. "Data Protection Laws" means the GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, and the US state privacy laws, each to the extent it applies; a reference to the GDPR includes the UK GDPR where that applies.

For the purposes of this DPA, Customer is the controller and Vendor is the processor of the Personal Data processed under the Agreement, within the meaning of GDPR Article 28. Where either party independently determines the purposes and means of processing any Personal Data, that party is a controller of that Personal Data and is separately responsible for its own obligations.

Vendor shall process Personal Data only on Customer's documented instructions, as required by GDPR Article 28(3). Vendor shall promptly notify Customer if, in its opinion, an instruction infringes applicable law. Vendor shall not process Personal Data to improve its own products or services without Customer's separate prior written consent.

Vendor shall ensure that all personnel who process Personal Data are bound by written confidentiality obligations, whether contractual or statutory, and receive training on their data protection obligations under the GDPR. Vendor shall impose equivalent confidentiality obligations by written contract on each sub-processor.

Vendor shall implement and maintain the technical and organizational measures described in its security documentation, which it shall make available to Customer. Vendor's current SOC 2 Type II report or ISO 27001 certification is evidence of its compliance with this section. Vendor may update those measures from time to time, provided that no update reduces the overall level of security of the Services.

Vendor shall maintain a publicly accessible list of its sub-processors and give Customer 30 days' advance written notice before engaging a new sub-processor. Customer may object to a new sub-processor on reasonable grounds. If the parties cannot resolve the objection within 30 days, either party may terminate the affected Services without penalty.

Vendor shall provide Customer with prompt technical assistance in responding to requests by data subjects to exercise their rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection, within 30 days of Customer's request. Vendor's obligation extends only to Personal Data held in Vendor's systems. Customer shall pay for Vendor's assistance with more than 3 requests in any year.

then.p: Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay, and in any event within 72 hours, after becoming aware of a Personal Data breach, so that Customer can meet its obligations under GDPR Articles 33–34. The notice shall describe the nature of the breach, the categories and approximate number of data subjects affected, its likely consequences and the measures taken. Where any of that information is not yet available, Vendor shall provide it as it becomes available.

Vendor shall notify Customer within 72 hours after confirming a reportable Personal Data breach, and no notice is required for a suspected breach. The initial notice may be partial, with full details to follow within 7 days. Vendor alone shall determine the scope and severity of the breach, and Customer is solely responsible for notifying supervisory authorities and data subjects under GDPR Articles 33–34.

Vendor shall notify Customer within 24 hours of any suspected or confirmed Personal Data breach, and the initial notice shall state the number of records and the categories of Personal Data affected. Vendor shall actively assist Customer in preparing its notifications to supervisory authorities and data subjects. Where the breach results from Vendor's failure or negligence, Vendor shall bear the cost of external breach notification services.

body.p: Customer security contact for breach notices: [[text:Customer:Security contact]]  Email: [[email:Customer:Security email]]

On Customer's written request, Vendor shall assist Customer in carrying out data protection impact assessments of high-risk processing under GDPR Article 35, including by providing documentation of the processing operations and Vendor's own risk assessments. The parties shall share the cost of Vendor's assistance with any complex assessment lasting several weeks.

then.p: Vendor processes Personal Data in the United States. To the extent the GDPR applies to Customer's transfer of Personal Data to Vendor, the parties incorporate by reference the standard contractual clauses approved by Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914, Module 2 (controller to processor) (the "SCCs"), with Customer as data exporter and Vendor as data importer, the optional docking clause included, option 2 of Clause 9 (general authorization) with the notice period in the Sub-processors section, and Clauses 17 and 18 governed by and submitted to the law and courts of Ireland. To the extent the UK GDPR applies, the International Data Transfer Addendum to the SCCs issued by the UK Information Commissioner (the "UK Addendum") also applies. Annexes I and II of this DPA are Annexes I and II to the SCCs.

Vendor processes Personal Data in the United Kingdom, which the European Commission has decided ensures an adequate level of protection, so no further safeguard is needed for transfers from the EEA to Vendor while that decision is in force. Where Vendor transfers Personal Data to a sub-processor in a country without an adequacy decision or UK adequacy regulations, it does so under the standard contractual clauses approved by Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914, Module 3 (processor to processor) (the "SCCs"), with, for Personal Data subject to the UK GDPR, the International Data Transfer Addendum issued by the UK Information Commissioner (the "UK Addendum").

Vendor processes Personal Data in Ireland, within the European Economic Area. Where Vendor transfers Personal Data to a sub-processor outside the EEA in a country without an adequacy decision, it does so under the standard contractual clauses approved by Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914, Module 3 (processor to processor) (the "SCCs"), with, for Personal Data subject to the UK GDPR, the International Data Transfer Addendum issued by the UK Information Commissioner (the "UK Addendum").

body.p: Vendor shall maintain a transfer impact assessment for each destination country, and give Customer 30 days' advance written notice before transferring Personal Data to a new destination country.
[[check?:Customer:Transfer impact assessment received]] Customer has received Vendor's transfer impact assessment.

On termination of the Agreement, Vendor shall return all Personal Data to Customer in a standard machine-readable format, such as CSV or JSON, within 30 days. Vendor shall delete all copies, including backups, within 60 days after the return and certify the deletion to Customer in writing. At Customer's request, Vendor shall provide a transition period of 90 days.

Customer may audit Vendor's compliance with this DPA once per calendar year on 30 days' written notice. Vendor may satisfy that right by providing its most recent SOC 2 Type II report or ISO 27001 certificate, but Customer may conduct an on-site audit where those reports do not address its specific concerns. The parties shall share the costs of each audit equally.

To the extent the California Consumer Privacy Act or another US state privacy law applies, Vendor is a "service provider" or "processor" under it and shall not sell or share Personal Data; retain, use or disclose it for any purpose other than the business purposes specified in the Agreement, or outside the direct business relationship between the parties; or combine it with personal information it receives from others, except as those laws permit. Vendor shall comply with those laws, provide the level of privacy protection they require, and notify Customer if it can no longer meet its obligations under them. Vendor certifies that it understands and will comply with these restrictions.

Each party's liability arising out of or relating to this DPA, whether in contract, tort or otherwise, is subject to the limitations and exclusions of liability in the Agreement, except to the extent the SCCs or Data Protection Laws do not permit liability to be limited.

If this DPA conflicts with the Agreement, this DPA governs as to the processing of Personal Data. If the SCCs or the UK Addendum apply and conflict with this DPA or the Agreement, the SCCs or the UK Addendum govern.

This DPA is governed by the law that governs the Agreement, any dispute under it is resolved in the manner the Agreement provides, and notices under it are given as the Agreement provides. This DPA is the entire agreement of the parties on its subject and may be amended only in a writing signed by both parties. It may be signed in counterparts and by electronic signature, each of which is an original.

body.h: Annex II — Technical and Organizational Measures

body.p: The measures in Vendor's security documentation, as updated under the Security Measures section, including: encryption of Personal Data in transit (TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (AES-256); role-based access with multi-factor authentication; logging and monitoring; annual penetration testing; backup and business-continuity procedures; vendor risk management; and personnel screening and training. Vendor's current SOC 2 Type II report describes them in detail.
